Residents oppose plans for 195 homes in Christchurch

15th November
Local government
People
Planning and development
Newport
By Nikita Singh Live News Reporter

Share

4 comments

Plans for 195 homes in Newport village branded 'countryside vandalism' (Image: Supplied)

Residents have raised concerns over plans for nearly 200 new homes in a village.

The proposals, part of Newport City Council’s Replacement Local Development Plan (RLDP), could see 195 houses built on two sites in and around Christchurch, with 120 homes proposed for land north of Old Hill and 75 on land north of Christchurch Hill.

Although still at the consultation stage and not yet formal planning applications, the proposals have already sparked strong opposition from the community.

Paul Chard, a resident of Christchurch, said: "This is nuts.

"There is no infrastructure in Christchurch to support almost 200 homes on top of what we already have.

"Belmont Hill and the Royal Oak Hill is already overwhelmed with traffic in the rush hour.

"Equally, Christchurch Road is a small residential road.

"How will all the new cars get in and out of the village?"

Another resident from Caerleon described the plans as "countryside vandalism" and said they were "really angry".

Concerns have also been voiced on social media, with Anne Wrathall commenting on the Open Caerleon Facebook page that the proposals would worsen congestion, pollution, and pressure on schools and GP surgeries.

She said: "This is just ridiculous.

"The council want to build on any area of green land and spoil these places."

She added that surrounding roads are "already congested at rush hour" and warned that hundreds of additional cars could add to the problem.

Christchurch is a hilltop village overlooking the Usk Valley, known for its historic Holy Trinity Church and village character.

Despite being within Newport’s expanding urban area, it has retained much of its village character.

The RLDP sets out where development—including housing, employment, and infrastructure—should take place in Newport between 2021 and 2036.

The plan is currently at the Deposit Plan consultation stage, allowing residents and stakeholders to submit feedback before it moves forward.

Michael Enea, a Conservative campaigner in Newport, has also criticised the proposals.

He said: "Any plans to ‘mass build’ new housing around the Christchurch village should be scrapped immediately.

"I fully accept we need to increase our housing capacity, but surely the council should be looking at old brownfield sites in areas such as around the Newport Docks or elsewhere?

"The endless erosion of greenfield sites has to end.

"I strongly oppose these proposals."

The inclusion of these sites in the RLDP does not mean planning permission has been granted.
